summary.title: Writing a Rust Roguelike for the Desktop and the Web
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a small ASCII roguelike skeleton in Rust with the Quicksilver engine that runs natively on Windows, macOS and Linux and in the browser via WebAssembly.
keywords: build native and web game from one codebase
how do i make a game playable in browser
takeaways: Set up a Rust project with Quicksilver so the same code targets desktop and WebAssembly.
Load a monospace font, render it to images once, and draw text and a glyph tileset on screen.
Model map tiles and entities with simple structs and build a grid map.
Handle DPI scaling artefacts by switching the image scale strategy from Pixelate to Blur.
summary.summary: This is a hands-on tutorial, originally written for the 7 Day Roguelike Challenge, that walks through building a small ASCII roguelike skeleton in Rust. It uses the Quicksilver game framework and cargo-web so one codebase builds for Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser via WebAssembly. The guide proceeds step by step: project setup, an empty window, loading the mononoki font, generating a tile map and entities, building a glyph tileset (sprite atlas) from the font, and drawing the map with blended colours. The page notes it is the original version and is no longer updated, pointing to a newer repository.
